### `models.py` — Task & DAG Models

```python name=llm_compiler/models.py
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum        import Enum
from typing      import Optional

class TaskStatus(Enum):
    PENDING   = "pending"
    RUNNING   = "running"
    COMPLETED = "completed"
    FAILED    = "failed"

@dataclass
class Task:
    """
    Represents one unit of work in the DAG.
    """
    id:           int                    # Unique task ID (1-indexed)
    description:  str                    # What this task does
    tool:         str                    # Tool to call
    tool_input:   str                    # Input for the tool
    dependencies: list[int]              # IDs of tasks that must complete first
    status:       TaskStatus = TaskStatus.PENDING
    result:       Optional[str] = None   # Output after execution

    def is_ready(self, completed_ids: set[int]) -> bool:
        """Returns True if all dependencies are satisfied."""
        return all(dep in completed_ids for dep in self.dependencies)

    def __repr__(self):
        deps = self.dependencies if self.dependencies else "none"
        return (f"Task(id={self.id}, tool={self.tool}, "
                f"deps={deps}, status={self.status.value})")

@dataclass
class DAGPlan:
    """The full execution plan as a DAG."""
    tasks:    list[Task]
    objective: str

    def get_ready_tasks(self, completed_ids: set[int]) -> list[Task]:
        """Returns all tasks that are ready to run."""
        return [
            t for t in self.tasks
            if t.status == TaskStatus.PENDING
            and t.is_ready(completed_ids)
        ]

    def all_completed(self) -> bool:
        return all(t.status == TaskStatus.COMPLETED for t in self.tasks)

    def summary(self) -> str:
        lines = [f"DAG Plan — {len(self.tasks)} tasks:"]
        for t in self.tasks:
            deps = f"deps={t.dependencies}" if t.dependencies else "no deps"
            lines.append(f"  Task {t.id}: [{t.tool}] {t.description[:50]}... ({deps})")
        return "\n".join(lines)
```

### `tools.py` — Tool Functions

```python name=llm_compiler/tools.py
import math
import time
from datetime import datetime

def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Simulated web search."""
    kb = {
        "latest ai trends":           "Top AI trends 2024: Multimodal AI, AI Agents, RAG, LLM fine-tuning, Edge AI.",
        "top ai companies":           "Top AI companies: OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Microsoft, Meta AI.",
        "azure openai features":      "Azure OpenAI: GPT-4o, Embeddings, DALL-E, Whisper, fine-tuning, function calling.",
        "python best practices":      "Python best practices: type hints, docstrings, PEP8, virtual envs, pytest, logging.",
        "benefits of cloud computing":"Cloud benefits: scalability, cost savings, reliability, global reach, security.",
        "population of india":        "India population: ~1.44 billion (2024).",
        "population of usa":          "USA population: ~335 million (2024).",
        "gdp of usa":                 "USA GDP: ~$27.4 trillion (2023).",
        "gdp of china":               "China GDP: ~$17.7 trillion (2023).",
        "machine learning frameworks":"Top ML frameworks: PyTorch, TensorFlow, Scikit-learn, JAX, Keras.",
        "best python web frameworks":  "Top Python web frameworks: FastAPI, Django, Flask, Starlette.",
    }
    query_lower = query.lower()
    for key, val in kb.items():
        if any(w in query_lower for w in key.split() if len(w) > 3):
            return val
    return f"No results found for: '{query}'"

def calculator(expression: str) -> str:
    """Evaluates math expressions."""
    try:
        allowed = {k: v for k, v in math.__dict__.items() if not k.startswith("_")}
        result  = eval(expression, {"__builtins__": {}}, allowed)
        return f"{expression} = {result}"
    except Exception as e:
        return f"Calculator error: {e}"

def get_weather(city: str) -> str:
    """Simulated weather lookup."""
    data = {
        "paris":     "18°C, Partly Cloudy",
        "london":    "12°C, Rainy",
        "new york":  "22°C, Sunny",
        "tokyo":     "25°C, Clear",
        "hyderabad": "35°C, Hot and Humid",
        "mumbai":    "32°C, Humid",
        "berlin":    "10°C, Overcast",
        "sydney":    "20°C, Windy",
        "dubai":     "40°C, Sunny and Hot",
    }
    return data.get(city.lower(), f"No weather data for '{city}'.")

def unit_converter(value_from_to: str) -> str:
    """Converts units. Input format: 'value,from_unit,to_unit'"""
    try:
        parts     = [p.strip() for p in value_from_to.split(",")]
        value     = float(parts[0])
        from_unit = parts[1].lower()
        to_unit   = parts[2].lower()
        conversions = {
            ("km",      "miles"):       lambda v: round(v * 0.621371, 4),
            ("miles",   "km"):          lambda v: round(v * 1.60934,  4),
            ("kg",      "pounds"):      lambda v: round(v * 2.20462,  4),
            ("celsius", "fahrenheit"):  lambda v: round((v*9/5)+32,   4),
            ("fahrenheit", "celsius"):  lambda v: round((v-32)*5/9,   4),
        }
        key = (from_unit, to_unit)
        if key in conversions:
            result = conversions[key](value)
            return f"{value} {from_unit} = {result} {to_unit}"
        return f"Conversion not supported: {from_unit} → {to_unit}"
    except Exception as e:
        return f"Converter error: {e}"

def summarize(text: str) -> str:
    """Simple summarizer."""
    words = text.split()
    if len(words) > 50:
        return " ".join(words[:50]) + "... [summarized]"
    return f"Summary: {text}"

def get_datetime(_: str = "") -> str:
    return f"Current UTC: {datetime.utcnow().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}"

# ─────────────────────────────────────────
# TOOL REGISTRY
# ─────────────────────────────────────────
TOOL_REGISTRY = {
    "web_search":     web_search,
    "calculator":     calculator,
    "get_weather":    get_weather,
    "unit_converter": unit_converter,
    "summarize":      summarize,
    "get_datetime":   get_datetime,
}

TOOL_NAMES = ", ".join(TOOL_REGISTRY.keys())

def run_tool(tool_name: str, tool_input: str) -> str:
    if tool_name not in TOOL_REGISTRY:
        return f"Unknown tool: '{tool_name}'. Available: {TOOL_NAMES}"
    try:
        return TOOL_REGISTRY[tool_name](tool_input)
    except Exception as e:
        return f"Tool '{tool_name}' error: {e}"
```

### `planner.py` — DAG Planner

```python name=llm_compiler/planner.py
import os
import json
from openai  import AzureOpenAI
from dotenv  import load_dotenv
from models  import Task, DAGPlan
from tools   import TOOL_NAMES

load_dotenv()

client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint=os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT"),
    api_key=os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"),
    api_version=os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION"),
)
DEPLOYMENT = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT")

PLANNER_PROMPT = f"""
You are an LLM Compiler Planner. Your job is to decompose a user task
into a DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) of sub-tasks for PARALLEL execution.

Available tools: {TOOL_NAMES}

CRITICAL RULES:
1. Tasks with NO dependencies run in PARALLEL simultaneously.
2. Tasks with dependencies run AFTER their dependencies complete.
3. Use {{{{RESULT_OF_TASK_N}}}} to reference output of task N.
4. Maximize parallelism — only add dependencies when truly required.
5. Return ONLY a valid JSON array, no explanation, no markdown.

Output format:
[
  {{
    "id": 1,
    "description": "What this task does",
    "tool": "tool_name",
    "tool_input": "input string for the tool",
    "dependencies": []
  }},
  {{
    "id": 2,
    "description": "Another independent task",
    "tool": "tool_name",
    "tool_input": "input string",
    "dependencies": []
  }},
  {{
    "id": 3,
    "description": "Task that needs results from 1 and 2",
    "tool": "summarize",
    "tool_input": "{{{{RESULT_OF_TASK_1}}}} and {{{{RESULT_OF_TASK_2}}}}",
    "dependencies": [1, 2]
  }}
]
"""

def build_dag_plan(user_task: str) -> DAGPlan:
    """Calls LLM to produce a DAG execution plan."""
    print("📐 Planner: Building DAG plan...\n")

    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=DEPLOYMENT,
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": PLANNER_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user",   "content": f"Task: {user_task}"},
        ],
        temperature=0.0,
        max_tokens=1200,
    )

    raw = response.choices[0].message.content.strip()

    # Strip markdown fences if present
    if "```" in raw:
        raw = raw.split("```")[1]
        if raw.startswith("json"):
            raw = raw[4:]

    tasks_data = json.loads(raw.strip())

    tasks = [
        Task(
            id           = t["id"],
            description  = t["description"],
            tool         = t["tool"],
            tool_input   = t["tool_input"],
            dependencies = t.get("dependencies", []),
        )
        for t in tasks_data
    ]

    return DAGPlan(tasks=tasks, objective=user_task)
```

### `executor.py` — Parallel Task Executor

```python name=llm_compiler/executor.py
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from models import Task, DAGPlan, TaskStatus
from tools  import run_tool

def resolve_inputs(tool_input: str, results: dict[int, str]) -> str:
    """Replace {RESULT_OF_TASK_N} placeholders with actual results."""
    for task_id, result in results.items():
        placeholder = f"{{{{RESULT_OF_TASK_{task_id}}}}}"
        tool_input  = tool_input.replace(placeholder, result)
    return tool_input

def execute_task(task: Task, results: dict[int, str]) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Execute a single task and return (task_id, result)."""
    resolved_input = resolve_inputs(task.tool_input, results)
    task.status    = TaskStatus.RUNNING
    result         = run_tool(task.tool, resolved_input)
    task.status    = TaskStatus.COMPLETED
    task.result    = result
    return task.id, result

def execute_dag(plan: DAGPlan, max_workers: int = 5) -> dict[int, str]:
    """
    Executes the DAG with maximum parallelism.

    Algorithm:
    1. Find all tasks with no unmet dependencies (ready tasks)
    2. Submit all ready tasks to thread pool simultaneously
    3. As tasks complete, mark them done and find new ready tasks
    4. Repeat until all tasks are complete
    """
    results:       dict[int, str] = {}
    completed_ids: set[int]       = set()
    round_num = 0

    print(f"⚙️  Executor: Starting parallel DAG execution...")
    print(f"   Total tasks: {len(plan.tasks)}\n")

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:

        while not plan.all_completed():
            round_num += 1

            # Find tasks ready to run
            ready_tasks = plan.get_ready_tasks(completed_ids)

            if not ready_tasks:
                # Safety check — shouldn't happen with valid DAG
                break

            print(f"  🔀 Round {round_num} — Running {len(ready_tasks)} "
                  f"task(s) in parallel:")
            for t in ready_tasks:
                print(f"     ▶ Task {t.id}: [{t.tool}] {t.description[:55]}...")

            start_time = time.time()

            # Submit all ready tasks simultaneously
            futures = {
                executor.submit(execute_task, task, results): task
                for task in ready_tasks
            }

            # Collect results as they complete
            for future in as_completed(futures):
                task_id, result = future.result()
                results[task_id]   = result
                completed_ids.add(task_id)
                print(f"     ✅ Task {task_id} done: {result[:70]}...")

            elapsed = time.time() - start_time
            print(f"     ⏱️  Round {round_num} completed in {elapsed:.2f}s\n")

    print(f"  🏁 All {len(plan.tasks)} tasks completed!\n")
    return results
```

### `joiner.py` — Result Aggregator

```python name=llm_compiler/joiner.py
import os
from openai  import AzureOpenAI
from dotenv  import load_dotenv
from models  import DAGPlan

load_dotenv()

client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint=os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT"),
    api_key=os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY"),
    api_version=os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION"),
)
DEPLOYMENT = os.getenv("AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT")

def join_results(plan: DAGPlan, results: dict[int, str]) -> str:
    """
    Joiner LLM aggregates all task results into
    one coherent, complete final answer.
    """
    print("🔗 Joiner: Aggregating all results...\n")

    # Build results summary
    results_text = ""
    for task in plan.tasks:
        result = results.get(task.id, "No result")
        results_text += (
            f"Task {task.id} — {task.description}\n"
            f"Result: {result}\n\n"
        )

    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=DEPLOYMENT,
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content":
                "You are a result aggregator. Combine all task results "
                "into one clear, complete, well-structured final answer. "
                "Be concise but comprehensive."
            },
            {"role": "user", "content":
                f"Original Objective:\n{plan.objective}\n\n"
                f"All Task Results:\n{results_text}\n"
                f"Write the final synthesized answer:"
            },
        ],
        temperature=0.3,
        max_tokens=1000,
    )
    return response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
```

### `agent.py` — LLM Compiler Controller

```python name=llm_compiler/agent.py
import time
from planner  import build_dag_plan
from executor import execute_dag
from joiner   import join_results

def llm_compiler_agent(user_task: str, max_workers: int = 5) -> str:
    """
    LLM Compiler Agent:
    1. Planner  → Builds DAG of tasks
    2. Executor → Runs independent tasks in parallel
    3. Joiner   → Aggregates results into final answer
    """
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"🚀 LLM COMPILER AGENT STARTED")
    print(f"📋 Task: {user_task}")
    print(f"{'='*60}\n")

    total_start = time.time()

    # ── Phase 1: PLAN ────────────────────────────
    plan = build_dag_plan(user_task)
    print(plan.summary())
    print()

    # ── Visualize DAG ────────────────────────────
    print("🗺️  DAG Dependency Map:")
    for task in plan.tasks:
        deps = f"← depends on {task.dependencies}" if task.dependencies else "← no deps (parallel)"
        print(f"   Task {task.id}: {task.description[:45]}... {deps}")
    print()

    # ── Phase 2: EXECUTE (Parallel) ──────────────
    results = execute_dag(plan, max_workers=max_workers)

    # ── Phase 3: JOIN ────────────────────────────
    final_answer = join_results(plan, results)

    total_time = time.time() - total_start

    print(f"{'='*60}")
    print(f"✅ FINAL ANSWER:\n\n{final_answer}")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    print(f"⏱️  Total time: {total_time:.2f}s")

    return final_answer
```

sections.title: Key Concepts Summary
sections.body:
| Concept | Detail |
|---|---|
| **DAG** | Directed Acyclic Graph — no circular deps |
| **Parallel Execution** | `ThreadPoolExecutor` runs independent tasks simultaneously |
| **Dependency Resolution** | Tasks wait for all deps before running |
| **`{RESULT_OF_TASK_N}`** | Placeholder resolved at execution time |
| **Rounds** | Each round runs all currently-ready tasks in parallel |
| **Joiner** | LLM synthesizes all results into final answer |
| **max_workers** | Controls thread pool size (default: 5) |

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: **LATS** is the most powerful agentic pattern — it combines **ReAct** (Reasoning + Acting), **Tree of Thoughts** (multi-branch exploration), and **Reflection** (self-critique) into one unified framework. It runs **multiple ReAct trajectories** as a tree, **scores each path** using a reflector, and selects the **best trajectory** to the final answer.
